chains.trait: Six jointed legs with a low, sprawled stance
links: Trait: six jointed legs with a low, sprawled stance
Why: stable on shifting debris requires low center of gravity
Why: forest floor accumulates deep, unstable litter
Why: 1.6 bar atmosphere traps heat & holds water vapor (F4, F18)

skill.effect: Moves 1.5× faster through root mats and leaf litter without sinking or alerting surface predators.

chains.weakness: Exposed on open ground; dense air makes running costly (F4, D16).

journal.en: Six legs for a world of three dimensions: roots, soil, and air.

plausibility.summary: A 4.2 cm, 0.8 g forest-floor detritivore on deep, wet litter (D28, F18) benefits from a low center of mass and many contact points on shifting root mats; 1.05 g and 1.6× drag (F4, D16) favor crawling over sprinting. Island radiation with empty invertebrate niches (D30, F27) can plausibly produce a hexapod litter specialist alongside Babosa.
fixes: A 4.2 cm, 0.8 g forest-floor detritivore on deep, wet litter (D28, F18) benefits from a low center of mass and many contact points on shifting root mats; 1.05 g and 1.6× drag (F4, D16) favor crawling over sprinting. Island radiation with empty invertebrate niches (D30, F27) can plausibly produce a hexapod litter specialist alongside Babosa.

analogues.organism: Wood cockroach / ground-beetle litter fauna (low, sprawled runners on decaying leaf pack); convergent low profile also in woodlice (Porcellio) though not hexapods.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Broad, translucent forewings for silent gliding
links: Trait: broad, translucent forewings for silent gliding
Why: minimizes energy expenditure on a caloric-poor diet
Why: relies on aerodynamic lift rather than power flapping
Why: air is 1.6 times denser than Earth's (D11, F4)

skill.effect: Drifts 30 m downwind on thermal updrafts, landing softly on canopy or forest floor.

chains.weakness: Heavy rain or strong gusts knock it from the air (F19, D17).

journal.en: Wings not for speed, but for saving every joule of a rotten diet.

plausibility.summary: Reframe skill as short silent glide/descent (5–15 m) from fallen wood or pluma de sombra stems to litter, optionally extended downwind only after climbing; drop ‘thermal updrafts’ or restrict to edge/gap convection. Keep forewings as glide membranes (tegmina-like), not power flapping.
fixes: Reframe skill as short silent glide/descent (5–15 m) from fallen wood or pluma de sombra stems to litter, optionally extended downwind only after climbing; drop ‘thermal updrafts’ or restrict to edge/gap convection. Keep forewings as glide membranes (tegmina-like), not power flapping.

analogues.organism: Gliding ants (e.g. Cephalotes) and arboreal gliding inacs—membranous spread for controlled fall, not hawk-like soaring; silent membrane flight vs noisy stridulation in many orthopteroids.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Chitinous mouthparts coated in alkaloid-neutralizing enzymes
links: Trait: chitinous mouthparts coated in alkaloid-neutralizing enzymes
Why: breaks down defensive red-veined compounds & tough cellulose
Why: high-altitude plants wash downhill with runoff
Why: strong UV at 2,000 m forces red-purple UV screens (D25, F25, F1)

skill.effect: Dissolves tough litter and extracts nutrients, bypassing chewing; bypasses plant alkaloids.

chains.weakness: Ineffective on fresh meat or salt licks; gut pH crashes on non-alkaloid foods.

journal.en: It wears the forest's poison as a tool.

plausibility.summary: Name skill ‘Enzyme leach’ or salivary pre-digestion instead of strong acid unless you add a sealed crop; limit bypass to decayed red-veined detritus, not live Vetirroja.
fixes: Name skill ‘Enzyme leach’ or salivary pre-digestion instead of strong acid unless you add a sealed crop; limit bypass to decayed red-veined detritus, not live Vetirroja.

analogues.organism: Generalist detritivores and dead-leaf feeders (e.g. some scarab and tenebrionid larvae) with gut enzymes and symbionts for polyphenols/alkaloids in senescent litter; not full fresh-plant specialist like milkweed feeders.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Antennae packed with chemosensory pores; active only after dusk
links: Trait: antennae packed with chemosensory pores; active only after dusk
Why: tracks food by molecular plumes in still air
Why: scent diffusion slows as air cools & stabilizes
Why: 26 h day & thick air cause cool nocturnal pooling (D18, F3, F4)

skill.effect: Locks onto litter plumes within 40 m, ignoring visual decoys and surface noise.

chains.weakness: Blinded by bright daylight; antennae clog in wet spray.

journal.en: It reads the dark like a map written in rot.

plausibility.summary: Reduce claimed 40 m lock to ~15–25 m for general rot plumes, up to ~40 m only in still, humid night air or fog (F16); note antennae clog in evening storms (F8) as additional weakness.
fixes: Reduce claimed 40 m lock to ~15–25 m for general rot plumes, up to ~40 m only in still, humid night air or fog (F16); note antennae clog in evening storms (F8) as additional weakness.

analogues.organism: Nocturnal cockroach olfaction (Periplaneta) and large-antennaed moths tracking low-volatility compounds; cricket/beetle crepuscular activity on litter.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

relations.note: Hunted by fruit-eating gliders that snatch them from the forest floor.

secrets: Nocturnal variant bonus applies: befriend attempts in darkness gain +12 charm.
Rare albinos exist: pale individuals avoid toxic red-veined plants but lose UV camouflage.
moments: When the fog lifts at dawn, you see them resting beneath a fallen leaf like discarded velvet masks, their wings still catching the last of the night's breath.
